name: 2008 Calumet Avenue — the Philander C. Hanford house (Jaffray & Scott, 1883), K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-2982 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 20.000, v -0.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.616 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2008 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_2008 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Calumet Avenue, the district's named context buildings off Prairie Avenue: East Twentieth Street between Indiana and Prairie, and Calumet Avenue between 20th and 21st Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet at full size (0.1859 m a pixel): the rear wall at column 1303-1305 (the draft's u 0), the Calumet front's stone face at column 1438 (24.1 m, the trace's 10.35 m behind the street line), the north wall at row 400.5 and the south wall at row 456.5 (10.4 m; the draft's 10.5 kept). The front's corner projection (rows 447-463) and the north flank's small brick projection (columns 1372-1405, rows 393-400) are not built (L-k01-2008-calumet-3790).

stories.note: Two storeys over a raised basement, under a third storey in the roof: the plate draws basement lights, the principal and chamber storeys, a cornice, and the roof storey's dormers above it (the building notice's 'two-st'y dwell.'); the 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the roof storey.

construction.note: The plate draws the Calumet front and the south flank in coursed, rock-faced stone over a rusticated base; the 1911 sheet faces both in stone (blue) over a brick body. K01's all-stone house lays the north flank and the rear in the same stone, where the sheet draws brick: a liberty (L-k01-2008-calumet-3790).

stone_front.note: Brown sandstone: the register's 'brownstone' (the T-1837 row frontage-35x-2008) and the plate's coursed ashlar with dressed bands; the plate is monochrome, so the colour is the register's. Three rusticated courses under the principal floor, as the plate draws the base (rows of deep-jointed stone from grade to the water table).

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor about 1.4 m over grade: the plate's basement lights stand in a raised base and the stoop climbs about eight risers to the porch (read through the front's 10.5 m width, about 50 px a metre on the rotated plate).

storey_heights_m.note: The principal and chamber storeys read about equal on the plate (the principal a little the taller), set at 4.0 and 3.8 m on the front's width as scale.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a stone front on a brick backing.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the kit's service brick, laid where an all-stone house has none showing.

street_front_trim.note: The plate draws a moulded cornice hood over the principal and chamber lights of the front: K09's corniced lintel.

wall_head.note: A moulded stone cornice under the roof, carried round the front and the south flank in the plate; round the north and rear, which it does not see, by the kit's rule.

roof_form.note: A steep slated roof rising straight from the cornice to a low deck, its lower faces near vertical and pierced by gabled dormers (the plate); K01's mansard, lower faces at 72 degrees.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck over the steep faces, which the plate does not see.

mansard.note: Off the plate: the roof's steep faces about 3.2 m high over the cornice; a gabled dormer over the entrance bay on the street face and two on the south face (one over the flank's projecting bay, one near the rear), each a pedimented stone face with one light; and over the corner pavilion a tall pointed hip roof carried up past the deck to an iron finial. Heights, pitches and the sash are read at the front's scale; the deck and the north and rear faces, which the plate does not see, are the kit's.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the steep faces, drawn coursed on the plate; the deck's tin is reconstructed.

entrance_bay.note: The plate draws the door under a columned porch at the front's north end.

front_bays.note: Two bays north of the corner pavilion, read off the plate at the front's 10.5 m width: a single window bay (s 4.05-6.9) and the entrance bay under its porch (s 6.9-10.5).

side_bays.note: The south flank's windows: a pair near the rear (the plate's triple lights under the rear dormer stand for it), the three narrow lights east of the oriel, and one by the pavilion; the projecting bay between carries its own.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the plate does not see the north flank.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no picture sees the rear.

sash_by_storey.note: Tall single lights, the principal storey's the taller, read off the plate's bay north of the pavilion.

basement_lights.note: Square basement lights in the rusticated base, under each window (the plate).

chimneys.note: Two tall panelled stone stacks on the south flank, the plate's: one just behind the corner pavilion and one over the flank's projecting bay, each rising well over the deck to a corbelled cap.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the plate draws no downpipe on the faces it sees.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06's two-over-two sash for the plate's lights behind blinds.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's entrance porch at the front's north end: round stone columns carrying an entablature and a balustraded balcony before the chamber window, over a stone stoop. K07's hooded porch on columns with its rail. The plate's flight runs down northward along the front; K07's runs straight out to the walk, a liberty (L-k01-2008-calumet-3790).

boundary.note: The plate draws the yard open to the walk, a stone post at the stoop's foot; the lot (75 ft, the 1920 sale notice) runs v -11.35 to 11.85 on the 1904 parcel.

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the kit's yard and flagged walk to the stoop.

bays.note: The corner pavilion: the plate's south end of the front, about 4.05 m wide, stepped forward of the bays north of it and carried up as its own block under the pointed roof, one wide light a storey over a basement light; 0.45 m proud (the plate's shadowed return). The south flank's projecting bay: the 1911 sheet's stone projection (s35xfp-calumet_2008-b1 p4, u 7.6-11.9, about 1.2-1.7 m out, its corners canted), which the plate draws two storeys high under a gabled dormer and the flank's west stack; built square (the sheet's canted corners not built).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's one-storey brick range behind the main body at its south-west (s35xfp-calumet_2008-b1 p6, the draft's r3): u -2.0 to 0, v 0.25-3.75. Its light and tin deck are reconstructed.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D) faced in stone (blue) along its Calumet front and its south side, with a canted corner projection and a small frame porch at the south-west'. Carried to 1904 on the T-2982 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: "Residence of P. C. Hanford, Esq., Chicago.—Jaffrey [Jaffray] & Scott, Architects. Paul C. Lautrup, del." Pen perspective. The Inland Architect and Builder, vol. II, no. 5 (December 1883), p. 147.
what_it_supplies: the storeys, the roof's form and the dormers' places
the front's three bays: the corner pavilion, a window bay, the entrance bay and its porch
the south flank's projecting bay, oriel and stacks
the stone's coursing and the cornice
what_it_does_not_supply: the plan: the 1911 sheet controls it
the north flank and the rear

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2982) onto the K01 frontage assembly by T-3790 (piece 1 of T-1940, the X02 package of the T-1837 programme): the plan off the 1911 Sanborn sheet 35 at full size, and the front, the south flank and the roof off Paul C. Lautrup's perspective in The Inland Architect and Builder for December 1883 (inland_architect_1883_12_hanford_plate), the house as Jaffray & Scott designed it for Philander C. Hanford. Every dimension is read by proportion on the plate at the front's width, not through a solved camera; T-3791 solves the camera and works the photo-match down. Liberty L-k01-2008-calumet-3790 says what is read, what is invented and what is built otherwise; docs/RESEARCH/k01-2008-calumet-3790/README.md is the review.
